i am so thankful that i was able to find dr. huang during this pandemic. he may have literally saved my life by making the correct diagnosis and getting me off the wrong medications that was prescribed by other doctors. 

in early february of 2020, i had an endoscopy done by a gastroenterologist, and about a week after, i started noticing some shortness of breath and also felt a swollen lymph node behind my ear.to make a long story short, fast forward to march of 2020, in the midst of the covid pandemic,i had difficulty breathing and a fever which led me to believe that i may have had been infected with covid19. ultimately, after my lab test result tested negative for covid but indicated klebsiella pneumoniae bacteria, i went to see a pulmonologist at ucla where an x-ray of my lungs were taken to rule out pneumonia. although, the pulmonologist from ucla did not listen to my lungs, he prescribed an antibiotic given the bacteria found in my nose, and asthma medication for breathing problems (even though i had tested negative for asthma couple of years ago by this same doctor) after my breathing condition did not improve, i reached out to a different pulmonologist in glendale who provided telemedicine consults. the second doctor prescribed more asthma medication and ultimately told me to take a repeated x-ray and repeat covid test after my condition did not improve. after the chest xray came out clean for the second time, the doctor in glendale told me he did not know what the problem was and told me to hang in there or go to urgent care. by this time, i had slept only 5 days out of the last 15 days and lost over 10 pounds because of severe breathing problems, sleep deprivation and no appetite. 

then out of desperation at 6:00 am, after having stayed up all night, i searched for another pulmonologist and fortunately found dr. huang on yelp and reached out to him by email. surprisingly, dr. huang got back to me right away and saw me the same day through zoom video conference. dr. huang patiently listened to my history regarding the onset of symptoms  and complaints and told me that if one of the asthma medication he prescribed did not improve my condition within the next few days, then he would see me to figure out what was going on. after symptoms did not improve, i went in for an evaluation and dr. huang actually listened to my lungs using a stethoscope and also conducted a lung function test himself. after a comprehensive evaluation and a lung function test, dr. huang told me that i likely had some form of upper respiratory infection before which may have caused breathing problems and fever, but at the time of his evaluation, my lungs sounded normal and i should not be having such severe breathing problems. he told me that what may be going on is that the asthma medication that i was prescribed was causing anxiety and panic attachs which was making my breathing problems worse - causing a vicious cycle - breathing problem so take more asthma medicine which causes more anxiety which makes breathing problems worse. 

after i was taken off the medication, my breathing problems improved significantly. although, it took weeks to deal with getting over the psychological component of having had breathing problems and panic attacks, i am now almost fully recovered. 

dr. huang was so patient, kind, and methodical in the manner in which he diagnosed my condition in the midst of the covid pandemic. it was so difficult to find a doctor who was willing to actually listen to my lungs during this covid pandemic and give me a correct diagnosis. i cannot thank dr. huang enough. had i gone several more days without sleep, i'm not sure if i would still be alive today.

about a month before our estimated due date the covid 19 pandemic hit, causing our hospital to restrict visitors and not allow doulas in the birthing space. shalin calmly and proactively navigated this stressful situation, creating a library of online resource videos and offering virtual support for families in labor once they reached the hospital. she helped us to reformulate our plan for labor and birth to adapt to this less than ideal situation - helping us to regain a sense of control and support and reduce anxiety. 

on our baby's birthday shalin supported us in-person as we labored at home and then seamlessly transitioned to supporting us virtually via zoom and text once we moved to the hospital. her support throughout our pregnancy and birth played a huge role in helping us to achieve the positive and empowering birth experience we had envisioned.

our family lost our mother in march of 2019. she was an amazing woman who never let anything rise above her top priority of caring for her family, especially my father, bill.

my father is a disabled veteran with crippling arthritis and knee problems and a multitude of health issues and needs. he is a diabetic that requires insulin, has lymphedema that requires daily treatments, needs medications four times per day and after a two serious falls, required someone to be with him while he transferred from chair to walker, walker to bed, etc.  

my father was from a generation where his wife cooked, cleaned, raised us at home, gave us baths at night, did the laundry, went shopping and had dinner on the table when he got home from work. as we grew up and moved on, my father grew older and his world became smaller as his ailments and medical needs became his focus.

my mother took care of him with tireless effort, literally, up to the moment that she died. when she passed, he was lost.  with our family spread across the globe (literally) and having families of our own, caring for my father was an impossibility given the degree of care that he requires.

we were referred to visiting angels who came to meet and evaluate my father and had him set up with care givers within a week.

it was an adjustment for my father going from a doting wife who cared for his every emotional and physical need to have caregivers who he did not know come to his home to cook and care for him, but he adjusted and accepted that this was his new reality.  we watched this unfold and took great comfort in knowing he was receiving the care that he needed.

there were some bumps along the way, which i sheepishly have to admit were caused mostly by my father's attempts trying to alter a situation to get his way instead of what was safe and necessary.  these situations were mitigated with great communication between my family, my dad and from visiting angels and resolved.

over the last year, his mobility has declined.  he went from requiring 12 hours a day of care to 24 hour care after falling in his bedroom at night while alone. he injured his shoulder, but visiting angels was even able to provide a care giver for several hours at night during the week while he was in his rehab center for companionship.

when we realized we needed 24 hour care, visiting angels amazed us with their ability to provide a live-in care giver. this allowed my father to fall into a daily routine with the same person (something extremely important to him). he found it very comforting to get to know someone who also got to know him.  unfortunately this scenario ended yesterday as my father, regrettably, has reached the point that he requires multiple people to transfer him which would put any single caregiver at risk so he has to be placed in a nursing home.

we had to say goodbye to kristin, his most recent and utterly amazing live-in care giver.  she was sweet, caring, a wonderful cook and dedicated and was very much part of the family.

if it weren't for visiting angels, my father would have probably ended up in a nursing home or an extended care facility immediately after his wife's death which would have been devastating as he would have had to say goodbye to her and to the life he had always known at home all at once.  however, visiting angels provided the means for him to stay at home, provide amazing care which allowed him to continue his life as normally as possible.

no one could ever replace my mom, but visiting angels gave us all peace of mind knowing they were providing the care we wanted to be able to provide my father on our own, but couldn't.  visiting angels gave my father the ability to carry on with his life for over a a year in the comfort of his home. i highly recommend them.

i'm retired navy, on medicare and social security.  my vision had deteriorated significantly due to cataracts so it was time for surgery.  i spent over a year visiting three (3) different cataract surgeons before deciding on dr. stolldorf at horizon eye care.  those surgeons included doctors jaben, rheinbolt and  kansupada, all from ceenta.  they all had great online reviews.  however i found them and/or their staff's to be arrogant, indifferent and condescending. i strongly do not recommend these doctors or ceenta for cataract surgery or for any of your eye care needs. 

so when i met dr. stolldorf and his staff at horizon eye care, it was like a breath of fresh air.  he was receptive, listened to my concerns and was not judgmental or dismissive, no matter how trivial my concerns may have been*.  we discussed my cataract surgery needs and agreed on a plan - distant vision in one eye, dashboard vision in the other eye.  not true mono-vision which i didn't want. we discussed the various lens options and costs, and having slight astigmatism in my left eye, he recommended a special lens which i declined due to cost.  so i have standard iol in both eyes.

the horizon eye care team executed and coordinated pre-surgery through surgery flawlessly. surgery is performed one eye at a time about 4-6 weeks apart.  i was extremely nervous during the first surgery.  dr. stolldorf and the superb staff at the huntersville novant outpatient surgery center did an extraordinary job helping me feel comfortable and relaxed during surgery.  the cataract surgery itself only took about 25 minutes and was painless.  i was very happy with the entire surgery process and experience.  

fortunately i had no post-surgery complications with either eye.  healing was quick and i was back to my normal routine after a few days' rest.  the vision change from cataracts to no cataracts was dramatic.  i didn't realize how awful my vision was with cataracts until after surgery on the first eye was completed.  vision was clear and colors were bright in the operated eye, whereas vision in the other cataract eye was a hazy, blurred with a strong yellow cast.  it was like i had a new eye!

after about six weeks my eyes were for the most part completely healed, though i stayed on steroid drops a few extra weeks for one eye that was healing slower.  it's completely healed now.  my vision is excellent, though if i had to do it all over again i probably would have opted and paid for an astigmatism correcting lens in one eye, since vision is slightly fuzzy in that eye.  my post-op vision wasn't perfect, but except for the slight astigmatism, it met all my expectations.

though i can function perfectly without corrective lens, i've opted to wear glasses to obtain the optimal vision for working both on computers and flying airplanes.  obviously my lens implants don't correct for presbyopia, so reading glasses are generally necessary for very small print, though i can read and use digital devices without glasses sufficiently if needed thanks to having one eye optimized for distance and the other optimized for dashboard vision.

the entire process at horizon eye care went very smoothly and effortlessly from the initial appointment to the last post-op appointment.  *except for my very last post-op appointment, and there are many, where dr. stolldorf seemed a little short with me over my many questions, the entire experience was flawless.  i strongly recommend dr. stolldorf and horizon eye care for all your vision needs.  

it's now eight (8) months since i had surgery and i'm experiencing no surgery related issues and my vision remains good.  if only i could eliminate a few large "floaters" i'd truly have new eyes.  the aforementioned review is solely my opinion - your mileage may vary.
